title: FairMedFM: Fairness Benchmarking for Medical Imaging Foundation Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating performance disparities (e.g., delta AUC, Equalized Odds, delta Dice Similarity Coefficient) between male and female patient groups in medical imaging classification and segmentation tasks.
Comparing medical image classification and segmentation performance across different age groups (e.g., <60 vs. >=60 years old) using outcome-consistency and predictive-alignment fairness metrics.

Measuring disparities in model accuracy and segmentation overlap between different racial and ethnic groups (e.g., White vs. Non-white, Hispanic vs. Non-Hispanic) using fairness metrics like Disparate Impact and Equal Opportunity.
Assessing performance gaps in medical imaging foundation models based on the patient's preferred language (e.g., English vs. Non-English) using outcome-consistency fairness metrics.
Evaluating segmentation fairness across different BMI categories (underweight, normal, overweight, obese) using equity-scaled metrics and fairness-utility trade-offs.
Measuring discrepancies in medical imaging model outcomes across different marital statuses (e.g., single, married/partnered, divorced, widowed).
Evaluating model performance parity between left-handed and right-handed patients in brain MRI segmentation tasks.
Benchmarking fairness in dermatological and other medical imaging foundation models across different skin tone phenotypes.
